tui.spectrum.measure_hint: drag the mouse across the spectrogram
tui.spectrum.theory_text: Leakage: a finite window smears a tone over neighbouring bins. Hann's main lobe is 4 bins wide, its side lobes stay below −31 dB. Δt·Δf ≥ 1/4π: a long window sees the tone, a short one the hit in time. Zero padding makes the grid denser but does not raise the resolution.
tui.spectrum.cancelled: Cancelled — press r to compute again
tui.spectrum.too_short: The window N = {n} is longer than the signal ({frames}): lower N with W
tui.explain.spectrum.window: STFT window: its length N sets the time and frequency resolution; w/W pick other lengths
tui.explain.spectrum.preset.wide: Wideband — a window of N = 512: sharper in time, coarser in frequency (Δf = fs/512)
tui.explain.spectrum.preset.narrow: Narrowband — a window of N = 4096: sharper in frequency (Δf = fs/4096), blurred in time
tui.explain.spectrum.hann: Hann window and the overlap of neighbouring frames; o changes the overlap
tui.explain.spectrum.axis: Frequency axis of the spectrogram: logarithmic or linear (key l)
tui.explain.spectrum.axis.log: log — logarithmic frequency axis: low frequencies are stretched, octaves are equal
tui.explain.spectrum.axis.lin: lin — linear frequency axis: equal bands in hertz take equal height
tui.explain.spectrum.harmonics: Harmonics of f₀ — find the fundamental of the selection and mark its multiples (key h)
tui.explain.spectrum.fold: ↓M — show where frequencies above fs/2M alias when downsampling without a filter (key m)
tui.explain.spectrum.floor: Floor — the bottom of the dB scale: anything quieter is background; [ ] change it by 10 dB
tui.explain.spectrum.panel.spectrogram: Spectrogram |STFT| in dB; click sets the cursor, drag a box, Ctrl+drag a selection
tui.explain.spectrum.panel.selection: Average spectrum of the selected span and its peaks
tui.explain.spectrum.panel.cursor: Time, frequency and level under the cursor
tui.explain.spectrum.panel.window: Window and resolution: Δt and Δf of the current STFT window
tui.explain.spectrum.panel.measure: Box measurement: the time and frequency difference between its corners
tui.explain.spectrum.panel.list: Peaks of the selection spectrum, or the harmonics of f₀, with levels in dB
tui.explain.spectrum.panel.theory: The STFT uncertainty trade-off in brief; F1 for the tutorial

tui.explain.spectrum.legend.selection: ▾ marks the peaks; with harmonics on, the multiples of f₀

tui.explain.spectrum.legend.measure: Drag across the spectrogram to draw the box

tui.processing.empty: Open a WAV on tab «1 Signal» or with o
tui.processing.coeffs_chip: band scale: up to 4λⱼ · drag — λ ×
tui.processing.signal_chip: grey — noise-free reference · a / b / x
tui.processing.theory_text: Sparsity: a signal has few large coefficients, noise is an even layer of small ones in every band. soft: c − λ·sign c when |c| ≥ λ; hard: c when |c| ≥ λ, else 0. Different band gains break alias cancellation: A(ω) ≠ 0.

tui.explain.common.wavelet: Wavelet of the filter bank; click to pick another one in the palette
tui.explain.common.edges: Edges — how the signal is extended past its ends for convolution; it sets band lengths and edge effects
tui.explain.common.edges.symmetric: symmetric — the signal is mirrored past the edge, repeating the end sample (as pywt); click for the next
tui.explain.common.edges.periodization: periodization — the signal repeats periodically: bands are exactly N/2ʲ long, but the edges may jump
tui.explain.common.edges.zero: zero — zeros past the ends: bands grow by (L − 1)/2 and the edges step down to zero
tui.explain.common.edges.reflect: reflect — mirroring without repeating the end sample: …, x₂, x₁ | x₀, x₁, x₂ (as pywt)
tui.explain.common.rule: How the threshold λ for the detail coefficients d₁ … d_J is chosen
tui.explain.common.rule.bayesshrink: BayesShrink — a threshold per band from the signal variance estimate λⱼ = σ²/σₓ; usually best by MSE
tui.explain.common.rule.visushrink: VisuShrink — one universal threshold σ·√(2 ln N): almost all noise goes, but the signal is oversmoothed
tui.explain.common.rule.sureshrink: SureShrink — each band's threshold minimises the SURE risk estimate; sparse bands get the universal one
tui.explain.common.rule.minimax: Minimax — the Donoho–Johnstone threshold σ·(0.3936 + 0.1829·log₂N): milder than VisuShrink
tui.explain.common.mode: How the threshold is applied: soft, hard or garrote
tui.explain.common.mode.soft: soft — values below λ are zeroed, the rest shrink towards zero by λ: smooth, but amplitudes drop
tui.explain.common.mode.hard: hard — values below λ are zeroed, the rest stay as they are: sharper peaks, but noise spikes remain
tui.explain.common.mode.garrote: garrote — the non-negative garrote y·(1 − λ²/y²): between soft and hard, large values barely change

tui.designer.roots: Roots of P₀(z) · click = move H₀ ↔ F₀
tui.designer.note.wavelet: both cascades converge: φ and φ̃ are in L² — this is a biorthogonal wavelet basis
tui.designer.note.diverges: PR holds, but the cascade over {filter} diverges: a filter bank without a wavelet basis
tui.designer.convention: h₁(z) = F₀(−z)    f₁(z) = −H₀(−z)    normalization Σh₀ = Σf₀ = √2
tui.designer.magnitude: Magnitude of H₀ ━ and F₀ ┅ · 0 dB at peak
tui.explain.designer.zeros: Zeros of P₀ at z = −1: ● go to H₀, ○ to F₀; ◂ ▸ move one zero
tui.explain.designer.header: Root table of P₀(z): the root, its multiplicity and whether it sits in H₀ or F₀
tui.explain.designer.group: Root group of P₀(z): click to move it between H₀ and F₀
tui.explain.designer.preset: Ready-made splits of the roots of P₀ between H₀ and F₀
tui.explain.designer.preset.daubechies: Daubechies — H₀ takes the roots inside the circle: minimum phase, the orthogonal dbN bank
tui.explain.designer.preset.max_phase: Max phase — H₀ takes the roots outside the circle: same |H₀| as Daubechies, reversed impulse
tui.explain.designer.preset.cdf: CDF — H₀ gets only zeros at z = −1 (a spline), F₀ the rest: a linear-phase biorthogonal bank
tui.explain.designer.preset.degenerate: Degenerate — every root in F₀, H₀ is a constant: PR holds formally, but H₀ filters nothing
tui.explain.designer.conjugates: Complex-conjugate roots always move as a pair so the coefficients stay real
tui.explain.designer.linear.phase: Linear phase — keep splits where z and 1/z̄ share a filter: both filters are symmetric
tui.explain.designer.orthogonal: Orthogonal — keep splits where F₀ is the time reverse of H₀
tui.explain.designer.wavelet.only: Wavelets only — hide splits whose cascade does not converge to a function φ
tui.explain.designer.roots: z-plane of the roots of P₀(z): ● in H₀, ○ in F₀; click a root to move its group
tui.explain.designer.checks: Bank checks: PR P₀(z) − P₀(−z) = 2z^−ℓ, orthogonality, linear phase and a convergent wavelet
tui.explain.designer.convention: How h₁ and f₁ are built from H₀ and F₀ and how the filters are normalised

tui.explain.diagram.wire.wo: wₒ — the odd phase after R(z)

tui.decomposition.all_on_hint: to edit bands, click ☑ on the left
tui.decomposition.empty: no signal · o — open WAV, : — commands
tui.decomposition.title.subbands: Subbands · ☑ = in synthesis · click the checkbox
tui.decomposition.chip.scale: |c| min/max · each band scaled on its own
tui.matrix.single_filter: «{name}» is a single filter: it has convolution, circulant and «Toeplitz + Hankel»; analysis and synthesis need a bank
tui.matrix.numbers_off: numbers — for N ≤ {n}, color for now
tui.matrix.dot: dot product of the row and x:
tui.matrix.note1: convolution = a row sliding over x;
tui.matrix.too_short: Multilevel W for {wavelet} (L = {l}) needs N ≥ {need}, now N = {n} — increase N with +
tui.matrix.levels_lowered: J = {asked} does not fit in N = {n} at L = {l} — showing J = {j}; J = {asked} needs N ≥ {need}
tui.matrix.levels_lowered_max: J = {asked} does not fit in N = {n} at L = {l} — showing J = {j}
tui.matrix.title: {name} · {rows} × {cols} · row {row} highlighted
tui.matrix.origin: Where A comes from: convolution T(h₀) → ↓2
tui.matrix.origin6: C(h) = F⁻¹ diag(ĥ) F → O(N log N)
tui.explain.matrix.filter: Filter or bank the matrix is built from; click to pick one in the palette
tui.explain.matrix.op: Which matrix to show: analysis, multilevel, convolution, circulant, synthesis or Toeplitz + Hankel
tui.explain.matrix.op.analysis: A = [L; B]: rows of h₀ and h₁ shifted by 2 — one DWT step, A·x gives a and d
tui.explain.matrix.op.multilevel: W — J DWT levels in one matrix: the approximation is split again, W·x = [a_J; d_J; …; d₁]
tui.explain.matrix.op.convolution: T(h₀) — the banded Toeplitz matrix of the linear convolution h₀ ∗ x, no downsampling
tui.explain.matrix.op.circulant: C(h₀) — circular convolution: rows shift cyclically and the DFT diagonalises it
tui.explain.matrix.op.product: S·A — synthesis after analysis; with PR it is the identity, and S = Aᵀ for an orthogonal bank
tui.explain.matrix.op.toeplitz_hankel: T + H — convolution with symmetric edge extension; the DCT-II diagonalises it (key t)
tui.explain.matrix.mode: Edges — how x is extended past its ends; this sets the size of A and whether it is orthogonal
tui.explain.matrix.mode.zero: zero — zeros past the ends: each band gets ⌊(N + L − 1)/2⌋ rows, so A is not square
tui.explain.matrix.mode.period: periodization — x repeats periodically: A is square N × N, and AᵀA = I for an orthogonal bank
tui.explain.matrix.mode.symm: symmetric — x is mirrored past the edge, repeating the end sample (as pywt); A is not square
tui.explain.matrix.order: Row order: all L rows, then all B rows, or interleaved L₀, B₀, L₁, B₁, …
tui.explain.matrix.order.blocks: [L; B] — lowpass rows (output a) on top, highpass rows (output d) below
tui.explain.matrix.order.interleaved: Interleaved — L and B rows alternate: the block-Toeplitz structure with 2 × 2 blocks shows
tui.explain.matrix.n: N — the length of x, the number of matrix columns; ◂ ▸ and n/N change it by 2
tui.explain.matrix.cell: Cell: colour shows each entry's sign and size, numbers show values when N fits; click or c
tui.explain.matrix.row: Highlighted row: its dot product with x is on the right; ◂ ▸ or ↑↓ move to the next one
tui.explain.matrix.panel.controls: Choose the matrix: filter, operation, edges, row order, N and cell view
tui.explain.matrix.panel.checks: Numerical checks of the current matrix: orthogonality, PR, singular values
tui.explain.matrix.panel.main: The whole matrix: a row is one output, a column one sample of x; click for a value, wheel zooms
tui.explain.matrix.panel.sigma: Singular values σᵢ on a log₁₀ scale; σ_max/σ_min is the condition number; s returns to the matrix
tui.explain.matrix.panel.origin: Where A comes from: every second row of the Toeplitz T(h₀) is kept — that is ↓2
tui.explain.matrix.chip.legend: Cell colours: blue is positive, vermilion negative, background zero; ◂ ▸ move the row
tui.explain.matrix.chip.origin: An example with N = 12 and no edge extension, so the whole band is visible
tui.explain.matrix.check.orth: ‖AᵀA − I‖ — how far A is from orthogonal; ≈ 0 only for an orthogonal bank with periodization
tui.explain.matrix.check.transpose: Synthesis S against Aᵀ: they match only for an orthogonal bank
tui.explain.matrix.check.inverse: ‖S·A·x − x‖ — the reconstruction error on the test x; ≈ 0 means PR
tui.explain.matrix.check.dct: How well DCT-II diagonalises T + H: what is left off the diagonal of C(T+H)Cᵀ
tui.explain.matrix.check.levinson: Solving T(r)·x = e₁ by the Levinson–Durbin recursion in O(N²), and its relative residual
tui.explain.matrix.check.gohberg: The inverse of the Toeplitz T by the Gohberg–Semencul formula, checked as T·T⁻¹ = I
tui.explain.matrix.check.singular: Largest and smallest σ and cond = σ_max/σ_min: how much A can amplify an error

tui.explain.resample.mode: Resampling mode: downsampling ↓M, upsampling ↑L or the rational L/M
tui.explain.resample.mode.down: ↓M — keep every M-th sample: fs′ = fs/M; without a filter frequencies above fs′/2 alias
tui.explain.resample.mode.up: ↑L — insert L − 1 zeros between samples: fs′ = L·fs; without a filter spectral images remain
tui.explain.resample.mode.rational: L/M — ↑L, one anti-aliasing filter, then ↓M: fs′ = fs·L/M
tui.explain.resample.m: M — the downsampling factor; − and + change it
tui.explain.resample.l: L — the upsampling factor; < and > change it
tui.explain.resample.filter: Anti-aliasing filter — a Kaiser FIR against aliasing at ↓M and images at ↑L
tui.explain.resample.filter.on: AA on — the filter is in place: aliasing and spectral images are suppressed
tui.explain.resample.filter.bypass: Bypass — no filter: you see the spectrum copies alias or the images remain
tui.explain.resample.cutoff: Cutoff of the anti-aliasing filter as a fraction of π/max(L, M), the lower Nyquist
tui.explain.resample.source: Input signal: a tone, a sweep or the file from the Signal tab
tui.explain.resample.source.tone: Tone — a single sinusoid: easy to see where it aliases after ↓M
tui.explain.resample.source.sweep: Sweep — the frequency rises over time: aliasing shows up as a mirrored line
tui.explain.resample.source.file: File — the signal open in the Signal tab
tui.explain.resample.panel.controls: Resampling settings: mode, M and L, anti-aliasing filter and input
tui.explain.resample.panel.before: Input spectrum at fs; with the anti-aliasing filter response if it runs before ↓M
tui.explain.resample.panel.after: Spectrum after resampling at fs′; with the filter bypassed aliasing and images show
tui.explain.resample.panel.readouts: Readouts: rates before and after, filter parameters and alias suppression
tui.explain.resample.panel.time: Samples before and after: ↑L inserts L − 1 zeros, ↓M keeps every M-th
tui.explain.resample.legend.after: How many spectrum copies X((ω − 2πk)/M) add up after ↓M
tui.explain.filters.role: Role in which a bank filter is added from the library: analysis or synthesis, low or high (t)
tui.explain.filters.role.h0: h₀ — the analysis lowpass: it produces the approximation a
tui.explain.filters.role.h1: h₁ — the analysis highpass: it produces the details d
tui.explain.filters.role.f0: f₀ — the synthesis lowpass: rebuilds the signal from a after ↑2
tui.explain.filters.role.f1: f₁ — the synthesis highpass: rebuilds the signal from d after ↑2
tui.explain.filters.group: Library group: click to fold or unfold it
tui.explain.filters.family: Filter family: click to list its filters on the line below
tui.explain.filters.filter: Click adds the filter to the comparison in the chosen role; added ones are highlighted
tui.explain.filters.entry: Filter in the comparison: click to focus it — impulse, zeros and properties follow it
tui.explain.filters.eye: Show or hide the filter's curve on the plots (Space)
tui.explain.filters.chip.db: dB — magnitude in decibels 20·log₁₀|H|: shows stopband attenuation (key d)
tui.explain.filters.chip.linear: lin — magnitude on a linear scale |H|: shows the passband shape (key d)
tui.explain.filters.chip.log: log ω — logarithmic frequency axis: low frequencies are stretched (key l)
tui.explain.filters.chip.normalised: norm. — each response is lifted to 0 dB at its peak so shapes compare (key n)
tui.explain.filters.chip.bands: PB / SB — the filter's passband and stopband; the transition spans −1 to −20 dB
tui.explain.filters.panel.magnitude: Magnitude |H(e^jω)| of every compared filter; click sets cursor A, b sets cursor B
tui.explain.filters.panel.phase: Phase response, unwrapped, in units of π; a straight line for linear-phase filters
tui.explain.filters.panel.delay: Group delay τ(ω) = −dφ/dω in samples: how much each frequency is delayed
tui.explain.filters.panel.impulse: Impulse response of the focused filter — its coefficients h[n]
tui.explain.filters.panel.zeros: Zeros ○ and poles × of the focused filter on the z-plane; an FIR has poles only at 0
tui.explain.filters.panel.properties: Properties of the focused filter: length, normalisation, symmetry and checks
tui.explain.filters.panel.measures: Automatic measurements from the magnitude: band edges, ripple and attenuation
tui.explain.filters.panel.library: Filter library: click to add to the comparison, / to search
tui.explain.filters.panel.comparison: Filters being compared: focus ↑↓, visibility Space, reference r, remove Del
pipeline.error.xcorr_rates: xcorr: the inputs have different sample rates — {a} and {b} Hz; bring them to one with the resample block
tui.explain.decomposition.view: How to show the decomposition: subbands, MRA, time–frequency tiles, packets or scalogram
tui.explain.decomposition.view.subbands: Subbands — the coefficients of each band d₁ … d_J and a_J over time; ☑ adds a band to synthesis
tui.explain.decomposition.view.mra: MRA — each band's share in the samples of x: x = d₁ + … + d_J + a_J
tui.explain.decomposition.view.tiles: t–f tiles — |c| of each coefficient: fine levels are narrow in time, coarse ones in frequency
tui.explain.decomposition.view.packets: Packets — the wavelet packet tree: both a and d split; click a node to make it a basis leaf
tui.explain.decomposition.view.scalogram: Scalogram — |W(a, t)| of the continuous Morlet wavelet: a smooth time–frequency picture
tui.explain.decomposition.transform: Which transform to compute: DWT with downsampling, or SWT/MODWT without it
tui.explain.decomposition.transform.dwt: DWT — ↓2 at every level: N coefficients in total, but the result depends on the signal shift
tui.explain.decomposition.transform.swt: SWT (à trous) — no downsampling, dilated filters: J + 1 bands of N samples, shift-invariant
tui.explain.decomposition.transform.modw: MODWT — SWT with filters h/√2: energy splits exactly over bands, any N, aligned bands
tui.explain.decomposition.levels: J — the number of levels: each level splits the approximation into two more bands
tui.explain.decomposition.check: ☑ — include or exclude the band in the synthesis B
tui.explain.decomposition.sigma: Noise σ — estimated from the median of |d₁|: MAD/0.6745, since d₁ is nearly all noise
tui.explain.decomposition.denoise.levels: Which detail levels get thresholded: d₁ … dₖ; ◂ ▸ change k, the approximation a_J is kept
tui.explain.decomposition.lambda: The selected method's threshold formula and the λⱼ per band once applied
tui.explain.decomposition.keep: Compression — keep only this share of the largest coefficients and zero the rest
tui.explain.decomposition.gain: Gain of the selected band in dB before synthesis; ◂ ▸ step by 1 dB
tui.explain.decomposition.processing.lin: Open Processing with the same wavelet and J: thresholds in detail and A/B/X listening
tui.explain.decomposition.play.a: Play the original signal A from the cursor
tui.explain.decomposition.play.b: Play the synthesis B from the ☑ bands, with threshold and edits
tui.explain.decomposition.play.x: Play the difference A − B: what the threshold and the excluded bands removed
tui.explain.decomposition.play.d: Play only the selected band — its MRA share
tui.explain.decomposition.play.cursor: One playback cursor for every view: playback starts from it
tui.explain.decomposition.panel.energy: Share of the coefficient energy in each band
tui.explain.decomposition.panel.cursor: Every band's value at the cursor; click the plot to set the cursor
tui.explain.decomposition.panel.denoise: Denoising and band edits: set them up and press Enter, u to undo
tui.explain.decomposition.panel.listen: A/B listening: the original, the synthesis, the difference or one band
tui.explain.decomposition.panel.summary: Synthesis summary: band energy share, reconstruction error and the Parseval check
tui.explain.decomposition.legend.scale: Each band on its own scale: from the minimum to the maximum |c| of that band
tui.explain.decomposition.legend.tiles: Tile colour is |c| in dB on the viridis scale; below −48 dB is background
tui.explain.decomposition.legend.packets: Node colour is its energy on the viridis scale; below −48 dB is background
tui.explain.decomposition.legend.scalogr: Colour is |W| in dB (viridis), below −48 dB is background; log frequency axis
tui.explain.processing.levels: J — the number of DWT levels; the threshold acts on d₁ … d_J, the approximation a_J is kept
tui.explain.processing.scale: λ × — threshold multiplier: below 1 keeps more detail and noise, above 1 removes signal too
tui.explain.processing.view: What the signal plot shows: A input, B result or X difference
tui.explain.processing.view.a: A — the input: the clean reference plus noise at the given SNR
tui.explain.processing.view.b: B — the result: synthesis after the threshold and band edits
tui.explain.processing.view.x: X — the difference A − B: what the threshold removed; ideally it looks like pure noise
tui.explain.processing.eq.flat: Flat — every band at gain 1, only the threshold acts
tui.explain.processing.eq.bass: Bass +6 dB — a_J and d_J ×2, d_(J−1) ×1.4: a low-frequency lift
tui.explain.processing.eq.no_d1: No d₁ — the highest band is zeroed entirely
tui.explain.processing.eq.notch_d3: Notch d₃ — band d₃ is zeroed: a one-octave dip
tui.explain.processing.play.x: Play X — what the threshold removed
tui.explain.processing.play.seamless: A, B and X play in sync: switching keeps the position
tui.explain.processing.panel.coeffs: Coefficients per band; the dashed ±λⱼ is the threshold: everything between them is zeroed
tui.explain.processing.panel.signal: The signal of the chosen view A, B or X over the noise-free reference
tui.explain.processing.panel.curve: The error when keeping the K largest coefficients; ● is how many the threshold keeps
tui.explain.processing.panel.eq: Band edits: gains and the overall response T(ω); ┅ is the aliasing from downsampling
tui.explain.processing.panel.summary: Summary: input and output SNR, coefficients kept, compression ratio and MSE
tui.explain.processing.panel.noise: Noise σ estimated by MAD(d₁)/0.6745, as in scikit-image
tui.explain.processing.panel.listen: A/B/X listening: the input, the result and the difference
tui.explain.processing.panel.theory: Why thresholding works: a signal has few large coefficients, noise is flat; F1 for more
tui.explain.processing.legend.coeffs: Each band is scaled to 4λⱼ; dragging across the plot changes the λ × multiplier
tui.explain.processing.legend.signal: Grey is the noise-free reference; a / b / x switch the view
tui.explain.processing.legend.curve: The axis is K, the largest coefficients kept; ● is the current threshold
tui.explain.processing.legend.eq: ━ is the overall T(ω); ┅ is the aliasing that band edits cannot remove
tui.explain.processing.legend.summary: The chosen threshold method and the λ × multiplier
tui.explain.processing.legend.theory: F1 opens the tutorial section on thresholding
tui.explain.explain.step: A walkthrough step: click to go to it; ←→ for the neighbouring step
tui.explain.explain.auto: Autoplay: the steps advance on their own; Space pauses
tui.explain.explain.bank.haar: Haar — the shortest bank, h₀ = [1, 1]/√2: everything can be done by hand
tui.explain.explain.bank.db2: db2 — Daubechies with 4 coefficients: orthogonal, two vanishing moments
tui.explain.explain.bank.legall53: LeGall 5/3 — the symmetric biorthogonal bank of lossless JPEG 2000
tui.explain.explain.bank.user: “Mine” — the last bank saved in the designer
tui.explain.explain.legend.scheme: w cycles to the next bank
tui.explain.explain.legend.story: The step invariant — what stays true after this step
tui.explain.explain.legend.matrix: [L; B] — lowpass rows on top, highpass rows below, as on the Matrix tab
tui.explain.explain.panel.scheme: The bank diagram at the current step and the sample table for an 8-sample x
tui.explain.explain.panel.steps: All walkthrough steps: click to go
tui.explain.explain.panel.story: What happens at this step and why
tui.explain.explain.panel.matrix: Matrix A₁ of one DWT level for N = 8: the same numbers as in the table
tui.explain.explain.panel.freq: Magnitude |H₀| and |H₁| of the bank on a linear scale
tui.explain.explain.panel.p0: P₀(z) = H₀(z)·F₀(z) and the condition under which aliasing cancels
tui.pipeline.no_free_inputs: no free inputs of a matching type
tui.pipeline.hint.connect_keys: connect: c — output, arrows, Enter; C — list of inputs
tui.pipeline.example.haar_bank: Haar bank: analysis and synthesis, as in «Explain»
tui.pipeline.example.dwt_levels: db4 DWT on 3 levels with a probe on every band
tui.pipeline.example.denoise: Denoise a file: DWT, threshold, IDWT

tui.pipeline.example.effects_chain: Chain: chirp, modulation, IIR and FIR, measurements, 9/7 lifting
